interest: This file offers a fascinating glimpse into interwar American intelligence gathering, showing how unsolicited rumors from private expatriate citizens reached the highest levels of the Roosevelt administration through personal networks—specifically FDR's confidential secretary Colonel Louis McHenry Howe. It reflects acute American sensitivities regarding foreign, and especially Japanese, geopolitical and naval encroachment in the Caribbean, as well as vigilance over potential violations of the Platt Amendment. Furthermore, Mrs. Montejo's letters provide vivid grassroots perspectives on the tumultuous political climate in provincial Cuba (Camagüey) following the collapse of the Machado regime, detailing the secretive operations, weapons procurement, and internal networks of revolutionary groups like the A.B.C.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.34537/1 and 894.34537/2) contains confidential correspondence from February and March 1934 between Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran of the Treasury Department and Under Secretary of State William Phillips regarding reports of a secret Japanese naval base in Cuba. The information originated from Mrs. Gail Hall de Montejo, an American woman residing in Camagüey married to a Cuban national, who alleged that corrupt officials during the regime of Cuban President Gerardo Machado had secretly sold naval base rights to Japan in violation of the Platt Amendment. Initiated at the suggestion of presidential advisor Colonel Louis McHenry Howe, the correspondence details local revolutionary figures in Camagüey (Dr. Louis Loasses and Paco Miranda), anti-Machado revolutionary intrigue, A.B.C. arms trafficking, and strict postal censorship in Cuba, while the State Department monitored and returned the transmitted materials.

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting an intelligence report from informant Gail Hall de Montejo to Under Secretary of State William Phillips.
subfiles.summary: Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran forwards to Under Secretary of State William Phillips a follow-up communication from Gail Hall de Montejo regarding an alleged Japanese naval base transaction in Cuba. Moran notes that while he is unsure of Phillips's interest in the writer's previous letter, he is transmitting this material for State Department review. Routing stamps indicate receipt and examination by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, the Division of Latin American Affairs, and Assistant Secretary of State Sumner Welles.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to William Phillips transmitting follow-up letter from Gail Hall de Montejo

subfiles.about: Informant letter identifying Cuban contacts with knowledge of the alleged Japanese naval base sale and offering intelligence on revolutionary arms smuggling.
subfiles.summary: Writing from Covington, Kentucky, Gail Hall de Montejo replies to Moran's acknowledgement and identifies Dr. Louis Loasses and Paco Miranda in Camagüey as sources with knowledge of Cuba's secret sale of a naval base site to Japan under the Machado regime. She asserts that corrupt officials pocketed most of the purchase money and omitted the transaction from official records, casting doubt on its legality. In addition, Montejo offers to collect information on arms procurement and financing by the revolutionary A.B.C. organization, while requesting strict secrecy and asking Moran not to reply directly to avoid endangering herself or alerting her Cuban husband.
subfiles.title: Letter from Gail Hall de Montejo to W. H. Moran regarding Japanese naval base rumors and Cuban revolutionaries

subfiles.about: Cover letter returning Gail Hall de Montejo's February 26 letter to the Secret Service Division after review.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips writes to Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran acknowledging receipt of his letter of March 9, 1934. Phillips expresses appreciation for the opportunity to examine the enclosure from Gail Hall de Montejo dated February 26, 1934. The enclosed letter is formally returned to the Secret Service Division with Phillips's reply.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to W. H. Moran returning enclosure from Gail Hall de Montejo

subfiles.about: Confidential letter transmitting Mrs. de Montejo's initial report on a Japanese naval base in Cuba to Under Secretary Phillips at the recommendation of Colonel Louis Howe.
subfiles.summary: Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran transmits an initial letter from Gail Hall de Montejo to Under Secretary of State William Phillips, along with a copy of his own reply to her. Moran explains that he is forwarding the matter confidentially and informally at the specific suggestion of presidential secretary Colonel Louis McHenry Howe. He offers to continue sending any further information that Mrs. de Montejo may obtain for the government.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to William Phillips forwarding report of Japanese naval base in Cuba

subfiles.about: Acknowledgement from Secret Service Chief Moran commending Gail Hall de Montejo for reporting alleged Japanese naval base negotiations in Cuba.
subfiles.summary: Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran writes to Gail Hall de Montejo in Covington, Kentucky, acknowledging her letter of February 18 concerning the rumored establishment of a Japanese naval base in Cuba. Moran expresses sincere appreciation for her patriotic initiative in alerting his office to the matter. He invites her to forward any additional information or details that she might obtain in the future.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to Gail Hall de Montejo acknowledging report on Japanese naval base

subfiles.about: Initial report from Gail Hall de Montejo alerting the U.S. Secret Service to an alleged secret purchase of naval base rights in Cuba by Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gail Hall de Montejo informs the Secret Service Department that while residing in Camagüey, Cuba, she learned of a secret transaction under President Gerardo Machado granting Japan rights to establish a naval base on Cuban territory. She emphasizes that as a native-born American married to a Cuban, her national loyalty comes first, and warns that such an agreement would violate the Platt Amendment and threaten regional security. She offers to seek additional details upon returning to Cuba, noting severe past obstacles with mail interception and strict postal censorship between November 1932 and May 1933.
subfiles.title: Letter from Gail Hall de Montejo to Secret Service Department reporting alleged Japanese naval base in Cuba

subfiles.about: Letter from Under Secretary Phillips returning Mrs. de Montejo's initial letter to Chief Moran and expressing interest in subsequent reports.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips replies to Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran's letter of February 21, 1934, returning the enclosed report from Gail Hall de Montejo. Phillips states that he read the document with interest and returns it for Moran's records. He adds that he would be very pleased to receive any further letters Mrs. de Montejo might provide concerning the Japanese naval base rumor.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to W. H. Moran returning Gail Hall de Montejo's initial letter
